_comment: Conformance hash vectors for the versionable Canonical Type Grammar. See GRAMMAR.md. Each vector: 'fields' maps wire name -> canonical type string; 'payload' is the ','-joined 'name:canonicalType' pairs with names sorted by Unicode code point and is the authoritative ordered form ('fields' key order is informational only); 'hash' is the first 6 lowercase hex chars of sha256(payload encoded as UTF-8). Optional keys: 'pythonOnly' marks constructs with no C# equivalent; 'mustMatch'/'mustDiffer' name vectors whose hash must equal / must not equal this one's. An implementation passes by rendering each field's native type to the canonical string, rebuilding the payload, and reproducing the hash.

vectors.name: no-fields
vectors.note: A schema with no fields hashes the empty payload.

vectors.name: single-field
vectors.note: Smallest non-empty payload.

vectors.name: simple-scalars
vectors.note: Two scalars, already in sorted order.

vectors.name: field-name-sorting
vectors.note: Fields declared out of order; sort is by Unicode code point (ordinal), so 'Mid' precedes 'alpha' precedes 'zeta'.

vectors.name: field-name-sorting-case
vectors.note: Ordinal sort puts all ASCII uppercase before all lowercase; a culture-aware sort would produce a different payload and a different hash.

vectors.name: worked-example
vectors.note: The worked example in GRAMMAR.md.

vectors.name: all-scalars
vectors.note: Every scalar token exactly once. Includes a standalone 'None' field; C# has no type whose sole value is null.

vectors.name: bool-is-not-int
vectors.note: bool is its own token; it never collapses to int.

vectors.name: scalar-width-erased
vectors.note: C# long/int/short/byte all render 'int'; float/double both render 'float' (ADR-0002). Python int/float render the same tokens.

vectors.name: complex-and-bytes
vectors.note: C# byte[] renders 'bytes' (carve-out from the array rule); System.Numerics.Complex renders 'complex'.

vectors.name: list-of-int
vectors.note: C#: List<int> / int[].

vectors.name: dict-str-float
vectors.note: Type arguments are separated by ', ' (comma + one space).

vectors.name: set-of-str
vectors.note: C#: HashSet<string>.

vectors.name: frozenset-of-int
vectors.note: C#: FrozenSet<int>.

vectors.name: tuple-mixed
vectors.note: Tuple arguments are order-significant. C#: (int, string, double).

vectors.name: tuple-mixed-reordered
vectors.note: Same members as tuple-mixed in a different order; must hash differently.

vectors.name: tuple-variadic
vectors.note: Homogeneous variadic tuple: the trailing '...' is the literal three-character token '...', legal only as the second and last tuple argument. Python tuple[int, ...]; no C# equivalent.

vectors.name: tuple-single
vectors.note: One-element tuple.

vectors.name: nested-containers
vectors.note: Containers nest without special-casing.

vectors.name: deep-nesting
vectors.note: Three levels of nesting.

vectors.name: container-of-serialization-name
vectors.note: Serialization Names appear inside containers unchanged.

vectors.name: optional-int
vectors.note: Python Optional[int] / int | None; C# int?. 'None' sorts before 'int' because 'N' (U+004E) < 'i' (U+0069).

vectors.name: union-sorting
vectors.note: Declared as Union[str, int, bool]; members are sorted by their rendered canonical strings, so declaration order is irrelevant.

vectors.name: union-none-not-first
vectors.note: None is NOT pinned to the front: 'Decimal' < 'None' ordinally. C#: decimal?.

vectors.name: union-none-middle
vectors.note: 'None' lands in the middle: Decimal < None < Path.

vectors.name: union-nested
vectors.note: Union members may themselves be containers; they sort by their full rendered string ('None' < 'list[int]' < 'str').

vectors.name: union-in-container
vectors.note: C#: Dictionary<string, double?>.

vectors.name: union-of-serialization-names
vectors.note: Serialization Names take part in union sorting like any other token.

vectors.name: enum-bare-name
vectors.note: Enums render their bare Serialization Name (ADR-0001) - NOT 'mypkg.config.Status'.

vectors.name: enum-explicit-name
vectors.note: An enum whose class is named Status but which declares the Serialization Name 'DeviceStatus'; the declared name is what hashes.

vectors.name: versionable-name
vectors.note: A nested Versionable renders its Serialization Name.

vectors.name: versionable-forward-ref
vectors.note: Self-referential schema; forward references render the referenced name.

vectors.name: datetime-family
vectors.note: Bare names, NOT 'datetime.datetime' / 'datetime.date' / ... . C#: DateTime|DateTimeOffset, DateOnly, TimeOnly, TimeSpan.

vectors.name: stdlib-converters
vectors.note: Bare names, NOT 'pathlib.Path' / 'decimal.Decimal' / 'uuid.UUID' / 're.Pattern'. C#: FilePath, decimal, Guid, Regex.

vectors.name: pure-paths
vectors.note: Pure path variants keep their distinct bare names (no C# equivalent in v1).

vectors.name: ndarray-bare
vectors.note: Un-parameterized array: dtype is dynamic. Python np.ndarray; no C# equivalent (Tensor<T> is always typed).

vectors.name: ndarray-float64
vectors.note: Python NDArray[np.float64]; C# Tensor<double>.

vectors.name: ndarray-float32
vectors.note: Same field name as ndarray-float64 with a narrower dtype; the hash MUST differ (ADR-0002).

vectors.name: ndarray-int32
vectors.note: C# Tensor<int> - note the array dtype is NOT width-erased, unlike scalar int.

vectors.name: ndarray-int64
vectors.note: C# Tensor<long>; distinct from ndarray[int32].

vectors.name: ndarray-uint8
vectors.note: C# Tensor<byte>. Not to be confused with byte[], which renders 'bytes'.

vectors.name: ndarray-bool
vectors.note: C# Tensor<bool>.

vectors.name: ndarray-complex128
vectors.note: C# Tensor<System.Numerics.Complex>.

vectors.name: ndarray-float16
vectors.note: C# Tensor<Half>.

vectors.name: ndarray-shape-erased
vectors.note: Declared in Python as np.ndarray[tuple[int, int, int], np.dtype[np.float64]] (a 3-D array). Shape is erased, so this deliberately has the same payload and hash as ndarray-float64.

vectors.name: ndarray-in-container
vectors.note: Arrays nest inside containers unchanged.

vectors.name: ndarray-optional
vectors.note: 'None' < 'ndarray[float64]' ordinally.

vectors.name: literal-strings
vectors.note: No 'typing.' prefix; string members are single-quoted.

vectors.name: literal-strings-reordered
vectors.note: Literal members are order-significant; must hash differently from literal-strings.

vectors.name: literal-ints
vectors.note: Integer members are rendered bare (unquoted).

vectors.name: literal-str-one
vectors.note: Disambiguation pair (1 of 2): the string '1'.

vectors.name: literal-int-one
vectors.note: Disambiguation pair (2 of 2): the integer 1. MUST differ from literal-str-one.

vectors.name: literal-mixed
vectors.note: Mixed string and integer members in declaration order.

vectors.name: literal-negative-int
vectors.note: Negative integers keep their leading minus sign.

vectors.name: literal-single-member
vectors.note: One-member Literal.

vectors.name: literal-optional
vectors.note: 'Literal[...]' < 'None' ordinally ('L' < 'N'), so None comes second.

vectors.name: annotated-unwrapped
vectors.note: Declared as Annotated[float, 'dB'] and Annotated[str, Field(...)]; Annotated metadata is ignored, so this hashes as plain float/str.

vectors.name: annotated-nested
vectors.note: Declared as list[Annotated[float, 'volts']]; unwrapping happens at any depth.

vectors.name: realistic-measurement
vectors.note: A realistic multi-field schema exercising most of the grammar at once.

vectors.name: realistic-device-config
vectors.note: A second realistic schema, converter-heavy.

vectors.name: literal-bool
vectors.note: Boolean Literal members render 'True'/'False'. Python checks bool before int (bool subclasses int), so Literal[True] never renders '1'.

vectors.name: literal-bool-vs-int
vectors.note: Companion to literal-bool: the integers 1 and 0 are distinct from True/False.

vectors.name: literal-none-member
vectors.note: A None member inside Literal renders the bare 'None' token (this is a Literal member, not a Union member — no sorting applies).

vectors.name: literal-enum-member
vectors.note: Enum-valued Literal members render '<SerializationName>.<MEMBER_NAME>'. Python-only; C# [LiteralValues] takes strings/ints.

vectors.name: literal-mixin-enum-member
vectors.note: Precedence lock (GRAMMAR.md section 8): the member is an instance of a str-mixin enum, so it is both an enum member and a string. Enum member is tested FIRST, so this renders 'Colour.RED', not 'red'. Source: class Colour(str, Enum) with RED = 'red', GREEN = 'green'; field annotated Literal[Colour.RED, Colour.GREEN]. A value-first implementation would emit the payload "colour:Literal['red', 'green']" and the hash fb5ba6 - a different, legitimate schema. Python-only; C# [LiteralValues] takes strings/ints.

vectors.name: literal-escapes
vectors.note: Escaping inside single-quoted string members: backslash -> \\ and single quote -> \'. Source values are: it's  and  a\b .

vectors.name: sort-by-name-not-pair
vectors.note: Sort-key trap: pairs are ordered by wire NAME, not by the assembled 'name:type' string. Sorting names gives 'a' < 'a1' -> a:str,a1:int. Sorting pairs would give 'a1:int' < 'a:str' (because '1' U+0031 < ':' U+003A) -> the wrong payload and a different hash. Applies to any name that is a prefix of another whose next character sorts below ':'.

vectors.name: parameterized-non-container
vectors.note: Declared as re.Pattern[str] and MyBox[int] (C#: Regex, MyBox<int>). Type parameters on types outside the closed parameterized set are dropped, so both render as bare Serialization Names.

vectors.name: non-ascii-utf8
vectors.note: Non-ASCII wire name and Literal string values. The payload is hashed as UTF-8 bytes, never UTF-16 — C# must use Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes. All characters are in the BMP, so ordinal and code-point ordering agree.
